To: Service Center Leadership
From: Service Operations Manager
Subject: Staffing Plan Review for Multi-Station Service Center

Overview
We are preparing the next-period staffing plan for our multi-station service center. Each station experiences its own customer flow measured per hour, and we have multiple staff types with different skills, speeds, and hourly costs. The core challenge is to place the right mix of qualified staff at each station so that customers are served promptly while we manage labor spend responsibly.

Situation
- Customer demand is known for each station as hourly arrival volumes.
- Staff handle customers at different speeds that vary by station and skill; these speeds are tracked as average minutes per customer.
- Not all staff types are qualified to work at every station, creating a structured set of allowable assignments.
- Each staff type has a limited number of people available and a distinct hourly cost.

Staffing Challenge
- We must assign people across stations in a way that matches each station’s expected arrivals with the team’s combined processing capability, without running staff at their limits.
- Because handling times are tracked in minutes per customer while arrivals are tracked per hour, we need to align these measures when estimating what a staffing mix can realistically process in an hour at each station.
- Some staff-to-station combinations are off-limits due to qualification restrictions and cannot be used.
- Each station requires a baseline number of staff for coverage, even when demand is light.
- Assignments across all stations must respect the limited availability of each staff type.

Service Policy Requirements
- Utilization cap: Staff should not be busy more than a target fraction of their time. Practically, this means the combined processing capability at a station should stay comfortably ahead of expected arrivals, leaving a buffer for variability, breaks, and ancillary tasks.
- Minimum coverage: Every station must have a floor level of staffing in place at all times to ensure operational continuity and safety.
- Qualifications: Staff may only be assigned to stations where they are trained and approved to work.
- Availability: We cannot schedule more personnel of any given type than we have available.
- Cost discipline: Staff types differ in hourly cost; we should meet service requirements while minimizing total hourly spend.

Objective
Build a station-by-station staffing plan that assigns qualified staff in the right quantities and mix to meet demand, maintain the utilization buffer, satisfy minimum coverage, and respect headcount limits—at the lowest achievable total hourly cost.

Next Steps
- Translate station-specific handling-time profiles into practical throughput expectations to compose teams that can comfortably keep pace with arrivals.
- Review proposed rosters with station leaders to confirm coverage for peak periods, coaching, and ancillary work.
- Stress-test the plan against reasonable variations in arrivals and staffing availability to confirm robustness.
